about.title: Rio Vista Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Rio Vista sits along Rt 12 and River Road, where local traffic mixes with drivers passing through Solano County toward the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. Public crash records show reported collisions on these corridors tend to cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., a pattern likely tied to weekend travel and shift changes. After any collision, insurers move fast, sometimes asking for a recorded statement before you've seen a doctor or understood what happened to your vehicle. Our team handles Rio Vista personal injury claims and can review the details of your crash, help you understand your options under California law, and handle communication with insurance adjusters. We focus on protecting your interests, managing the paperwork and deadlines, so you can focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Rio Vista Residents Choose Us

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Doesn't Wait
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, though claims involving a government entity — such as a road maintained by Caltrans or Solano County — can require notice in as little as six months. Reaching out early helps preserve your options before that window closes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Bar Your Claim
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you're partly responsible for what happened on Rt 12 or Main Street. We can help make sure fault is assessed fairly rather than accepted at face value.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California doesn't limit compensation for pain, suffering, or loss of enjoyment of life in most car accident cases. Our team can help account for these losses rather than letting an insurer set the terms.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early statements, made before you know the full extent of your injuries, to minimize what they eventually offer. Our team can advise you on what, if anything, to share.

items.question: What if my accident happened on Rt 12 or River Road and involved a public road issue?
items.answer: If a claim might involve a government entity, such as Caltrans or Solano County for road design or maintenance, California law can require a formal claim notice within as little as six months rather than the usual two years. It's worth having us review the specifics of where and how the crash happened as soon as possible.

items.question: How much does it cost to work with us?
items.answer: We offer free case reviews, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed.
